No license check exists anywhere in the code. Each phase ends when
its "real" list has been done against real systems, not when the code compiles.

## 0.1.0, the MVP

Built. The engine, durable executions, the Postgres queue and workers,
expressions, the Code step in its jail, the credential vault and OAuth2,
webhooks, schedules and MQTT, users with enforced MFA, OIDC, projects and RBAC,
audit, version history, the API, the editor, the connectors on the approved
list, workflow import, metrics and traces, the Helm chart and the Quadlet units.
Cut by `RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`, not before.

## 0.2.0, identity and governance

Built, and shipped inside 1.0.0 with the new editor. SAML, LDAP and AD, SCIM,
custom roles, external secrets, log streaming, variables, folders, insights,
execution annotations, the S3 and Azure blob backends, and execution redaction
policies. Each one is tried against the real server it talks to, and each has a
screen in the editor.

## What 1.0.x shipped

1.0.0 is 0.1.0 plus 0.2.0 plus the new editor, and nothing else. I called it 1.0.0
because the editor was the last piece I wanted before I put my name under the
number, not because everything below is done.

1.0.1 fixed one mistake in sign-in: a database that couldn't be read used to answer
"not signed in" and clear the cookie, so a short outage signed everyone out and
could turn a good second factor into a wrong code. It answers "try again" now and
keeps the session. 1.0.2 let a Code step sign and verify with an HMAC key kept as a
credential, and let a webhook name the web origins that may call it from a
browser. Nothing migrated between 1.0.0 and 1.0.2.

What a saved workflow holds to today: the file says which version of its format it
is (`cascade: 1`), every step carries its own version, and a workflow that names a
step that no longer exists fails to validate and does not start, instead of being
quietly changed. That is how the EmberOps steps were taken out in 1.0.0. There is
no promise yet about the format or the API beyond that, and no upgrade test from
every earlier release: what is tested is in `RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`, which upgrades
from the last release by hand. A promise goes here when I can keep it, and not
before.

## 1.2.0, the MCP server's last four tools

Built. The MCP server had four routes left out that a key may call: listing and
revoking your own keys, opening a workflow's test webhook, and starting an OAuth2
sign-in. They are tools now, 83 in all, each through its route, so the same
permission checks as the editor apply. The ten routes that want a person signed
in (making keys, SCIM tokens, secret providers and log destinations, and your own
password) stay out, because a key that could make them could keep itself alive;
the MCP page says which and why.

## 1.1.0, MCP and the missing screens

Built, and this is the release. The MCP server at `/mcp`: 79 tools, each one a
route of the REST API, so the route's own handler checks the permission, validates
the body, makes the change and writes the audit row. It ships on, with read and
write, like every MCP in the HotLoop family, and the two switches for it are the
deployment's own (`HOTLOOP_CASCADE_MCP`, `HOTLOOP_CASCADE_MCP_WRITES`), which no
tool and no route can change. The MCP page has every tool and what it asks for.

And the screens the editor was missing: Credentials, Projects (members and
service accounts), Users, the audit log, Settings and an Account page with API
keys, each with the same permissions as the API and tried in a real browser as
every role. The sign-in page is the editor's now, in its colors and type, and not
the old Go page.

## Not built: environments and scale

Built from this phase: the webhook role (its own Deployment in the split shape
of the chart), a concurrency limit per workflow, and many mains against one
database. What I have not done is the test I set for this phase, killing a main
during a minute-level schedule and finding no duplicate and no missed run over an
hour.

Not built, not scheduled:

- Git source control and environments.
- Protected instances.
- Rate limit controls.
- Retention: nothing prunes finished executions today, so they stay until
  somebody deletes them.
- Backup and restore.

## Not built: connectors and people

The connectors on the approved list that were built are in: HTTP, ntfy, Discord,
Gotify, email, HotLoop, MQTT, databases, files, and the S3 and Azure blob
stores. The EmberOps connector was in 0.1.x and is gone in 1.0.0.

Not built, not scheduled:

- The published declarative connector spec.
- A plugin SDK and an index.
- Forms with human approval steps. Approvals have to work from a phone, because
  the person approving a recipe change is standing at the line, not sitting at a
  desk.

## Not built: AI steps

LLM and agent steps, and a builder that uses your own model. Bring your own key or
run it local. None of it exists yet, and nobody has scheduled it. There is no
hosted service and there won't be one. (The MCP server, which lets an agent work
Cascade from outside, is built: see 1.1.0.)

## The new editor UI

Built, and in 1.0.0. The editor is rewritten in Astro with Svelte islands, built to
static assets and embedded in the Go binary the way the old one was, so it is the
same one-binary story with nothing new to run. It takes its colors, type and mark
from the HotLoop brand files, and follows the system's light or dark. Every screen
the old editor had is in it and does what it did (the canvas code came across
unchanged), the 0.2.0 features have screens, and a browser test drives each of
them against the real server in a real Chrome. Nothing about it changed the API,
the file format or the Go side.
